# Essay Stats MCP

> An MCP server with offline writing metrics for essays. It counts words and pages, scores readability, flags style problems and checks word limits. No account, no API key, no network.

Package: essay-stats-mcp (npm). Registry name: io.github.AnonymousOnyx22/essay-stats-mcp. Runs over stdio. Needs Node.js 20 or newer.

## Install

Add this to the MCP config of Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or Windsurf:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "essay-stats": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "essay-stats-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

VS Code uses a `servers` key instead of `mcpServers`.

## Tools

All tools are read only and work on text passed in the call.

- count_text: words, characters, sentences, paragraphs, reading time and estimated pages. Inputs: text, optional font (times new roman, arial, calibri, georgia, courier new, verdana), font_size (default 12) and spacing (single, 1.5, double; default double).
- readability_scores: Flesch Kincaid grade, Flesch reading ease, Gunning Fog and SMOG. Input: text. SMOG is marked less reliable under 30 sentences.
- style_flags: passive voice, repeated sentence openers, filler words and long sentences. Inputs: text, optional max_sentence_words (default 30).
- check_word_limit: compares text with a limit. Inputs: text, limit, optional minimum, tolerance_percent, exclude_references and exclude_quotes. Returns a status of under_minimum, within_limit, within_tolerance or over_limit.

## Example prompts

- "Count the words in this essay and estimate the pages in Times New Roman 12 double spaced."
- "Give me the Flesch Kincaid, Gunning Fog and SMOG scores for this paper."
- "Flag passive voice and filler words in my draft."
- "Is this under 2000 words if I leave out the works cited and quotes?"

## Privacy

Everything runs locally. The server makes no network requests and stores nothing. No keys or passwords are needed.
